scope: T07 Session/context boundaries; real SQLite/coordinator/runtime, fake backend evidence only, no models
checks: Cold native input requires trusted quiescent terminal evidence; anchor replay and a fresh SQLite connection restore the same native identity across Invocations.
API Sessions remain reconstructable metadata with no native ID, resume token or SDK anchor capability.
Two SQLite connections enforce Session CAS: a stale writer cannot replace the winning native identity or append an orphan context version.
Backend version, model, workspace, information boundary, account config/credential/native identity generation, permission and role/tool changes each create a fresh retained native identity.
Only included, authorized published sources become possible exposure; private/draft text and another member or owner anchor never cross the Session boundary.
Recursive source authorization is rechecked across Threads even when local permissions stay unchanged; revoked history forces a new Session and hides the old anchor.
Unknown execution retains its real claim; neither unconfirmed input nor an explicit cold boundary may silently rotate the active native identity.
A successful transport delivery without a trusted terminal anchor remains possible exposure and cold-starts after resource release.
An unexpected backend UUID durably marks reconciliation while preserving the original native ID and lock; no automatic replacement or false anchor is recorded.
Compaction requires verified native evidence and authorized source provenance; only a terminal anchor covering the exact boundary may resume.
Seal is an immutable idempotent boundary; it blocks further input and rotates identity only after the old claim is safely released.
Restoring an older Wake cutoff cannot reuse native memory containing later messages; the new cutoff produces a cold identity after safe release.
Possible exposure and context sending share one transaction; write failures roll back both, and failed anchors never become recoverable facts.
